pr_comments: Hi, i'm sorry for asking. Would it be possible to get this merged into the 2023.1 release? I'm not a developer myself, so i cannot help in the coding part. But i could help in testing.

The reason it previously went through the state machine was to guarantee that the state of min_max would actually contain every value it should represent. Now if 3 things change close to one another, one is unable to automate on the min_max value after only the first change.

That's correct but is it a behavior we would like to maintain?
It's also not in the documentation except for the attributes but their behavior doesn't change by this implementation.

A real solution would be to change architecture (see the last two posts of https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/83284 ), so that there is a clear distinction between the functional timestamp and the processing timestamp.
Assuming that is not a small task to do, we have to take the pain somewhere until that is possible. The current implemention in prod is causing database polution by plotting sensor data on the wrong day. This happens almost daily and is not a theoretical thing (see the screenshot below for an example).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/74881023/210278698-c66f2280-cca3-47a3-8dec-cd5f31a944ac.png)

I would suggest to move forward with the current pr and think of architectural options for an elegant solution.

@gjohansson-ST I don't know. But if we do, we should do so intentionally.

@pimw1 You're suggesting to move forward because you think it will fix your issue. However, it would still plot too late and pollute your DB + this change might break someone's else use case. We can't rush things.

@balloob From my side it's intentional as I would like to see the behavior same as for templates to always consider all available states. I would believe a user in such case would have automated on the attributes and those hasn't changed their behavior so I would believe the impact is minor.
@emontnemery thoughts?

issue_context.title: Helper [Combine the state of several sensors] is updating too late
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The new helper [Combine the state of several sensors] is updating too late (or too soon???).

See below query. I'm using the DSMR integration with tarif 1 and tarif 2. On top of that, utility meter weekly cycles are created. 

Both values were summed in the past via a template (see below, commented out now due to new setup). This was running succesfully for 1.5 years.

```
sensor:
'''
  #  for the p1 cable for the energy/gas meter
  - platform: template
    sensors:
      # weekly_energy:
      #   friendly_name: Weekly Energy
      #   unit_of_measurement: kWh
      #   unique_id: 5dc15de1-0653-4073-844d-8d91e485b5ec
      #   value_template: "{{ states('sensor.weekly_energy_offpeak') |default(0) |float(0) + states('sensor.weekly_energy_peak') |default(0) |float(0) }}"
```

However, since i switched to the new method [Combine the state of several sensors], the summation is going too slow:


```
select id
,time
,case when entity_id ='sensor.weekly_energy_offpeak' then state else null end as weekly_offpeak
,case when entity_id ='sensor.weekly_energy_peak' then state else null end as weekly_peak
,case when entity_id ='sensor.weekly_energy' then state else null end as weekly_total
from ltss
where entity_id in ( 'sensor.weekly_energy_offpeak', 'sensor.weekly_energy_peak','sensor.weekly_energy')
and time BETWEEN '2022-12-04 23:59:50'::timestamp and '2022-12-05 00:00:10'::timestamp
order by time asc;
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/74881023/205617628-a79b3fd4-5f63-486f-ba63-57809a4c846d.png)

Expected result: value 0 at 00:00:00. Instead, it is showing 25.601 at 00:00:00.

I've changed nothing in the utility meter. The only thing that changed, is me changing from the value_template in configuration.yaml to the new helper [Combine the state of several sensors]
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/74881023/205618134-d6c59e3b-ebc8-4cbb-8b9f-c19c846bc8da.png)



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.12.0b3

Home Assistant OS

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Another example of last night: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/74881023/205851486-70a15269-824f-422e-9f20-3ca2b39f796a.png)
The timestamps in this example are more spread in time, making it somewhat simpler to see what is going on.
edit: in this second example it is about a daily cycle, despite the column names stating otherwise

Below is a printscreen from the desired before-situation, when i was making use of the value_template.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/74881023/205894219-90892d1c-6a46-4d18-8190-14909a967c18.png)

@pimw1 To help debug this, it would be very helpful if you could:
- Configure a template sensor (which is updating correctly)
- Configure a min_max sensor (which is updating too slow), with the same input sensors as the template sensor
- Enable core debug log

Then share a log here which shows a case where the template sensor updates but the min_max sensor either didn't update or updated later than expected.

```yaml
logger:                       
  default: info               
  logs:                       
    homeassistant.core: debug
```

The problem is a race between the utility meter sensors when they reset, and the update of the `min_max` and `template` sensors.

- `min_max` will *always* have one corresponding state change for each state change of an input sensor because it has a local cache of input sensor states
- `template` *may* bundle state changes together, because it polls the state of its input sensors when it updates

There's no guarantee that the `template` sensor will not behave the same as the `min_max` sensor, but due to its design it will happen more rarely.

@pimw1 Can you explain why the two state changes are a problem for you?
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14281572/206167623-5de9061d-4c6d-4f7f-8f52-47e921660648.png)

Thank you for taking your time to look into this. It's much appreciated.

Regarding your questions:
Q: Can you explain why the two state changes are a problem for you?
A: i'm making use of TimeScaleDB, which makes aggregated "chunks" on a  daily interval (in my case). Those chunks aggregate the maximum value found within that chunk period. The current situation has direct impact on my grafana energy dashboards: end-result is a bar graph that is showing a high incorrect value for the new day directly after 00:00. This will retain this value until either a) a new day arrives or b) a higher energy value will ocur during the new day.

Q: To help debug this, it would be very helpful if you could:

Configure a template sensor (which is updating correctly)
Configure a min_max sensor (which is updating too slow), with the same input sensors as the template sensor
Enable core debug log.
Then share a log here which shows a case where the template sensor updates but the min_max sensor either didn't update or updated later than expected.
A: i noticed that gjohansson-ST created https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/83465 after this initial question
Is your question still relevant or would this fix the root cause? If still relevant, i'm more than happy to provide the debug log.

@pimw1 no, don't worry about the logs, it's no longer needed.

> i'm making use of TimeScaleDB, which makes aggregated "chunks" on a daily interval (in my case). Those chunks aggregate the maximum value found within that chunk period. The current situation has direct impact on my grafana energy dashboards: end-result is a bar graph that is showing a high incorrect value for the new day directly after 00:00. This will retain this value until either a) a new day arrives or b) a higher energy value will ocur during the new day.

Unfortunately, that's not a robust method and is not guaranteed to work. As I tried to explain above, it will work most of the time for your `template` sensor, but every once in a while, your template sensor may *also* give an additional state change.

The change in #83465 will make the behavior of the `min_max` sensor more similar to the `template` sensor.

Thanks Erik. I'm aware it's not a robuust method. In my personal situation, it should be ' good enough'  since i did not see this behaviour occuring in 1.5 years.

From a functional perspective, we could think about a different design (although not high priority). This is a typical example that is mathematically correct, but functionaly not, because:
-utility meter cycles are not physical sensors. they are virtual and designed to reset at 00:00
-the summation of the utility cycles are virtual as well. But the way that home assistant is handling the summation, is more in line with physical sensors that could update in different points in time (which is not the case here).

While thinking about it: perhaps a full solution would be to look into the behaviour of the utility sensors themselve: they should give a value at 00:00:00, not 00:00:00 plus some random miliseconds processing time. It looks to me that we are using metadata (processing datetime) to fill a functional datetime attribute (which is by definition exactly 00:00:00).

> the way that home assistant is handling the summation, is more in line with physical sensors that could update in different points in time (which is not the case here)

Yes, you're absolutely right. This is a very fundamental constraint of Home Assistant though, meaning it would require a fundamental architecture change to change it.

Having said that, accessing historic data of sensors during some well-defined period, such as a calendar week, is a common use case which I think is currently too difficult to achieve with Home Assistant.
The lovelace statistics graph card does allow displaying weekly usage (set "period" to "week" and "stat type" to "change"), but it doesn't allow you to stack or sum data from multiple sensors; they will instead be shown side-by-side.

There hasn't been any activity on this issue recently. Due to the high number of incoming GitHub notifications, we have to clean some of the old issues, as many of them have already been resolved with the latest updates.
Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue has now been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
